prerequisites: Basic concepts of signal and telecommunications theory.

learning_outcomes.text: To know and understand the current status and future trends of telecommunication standards, to prepare the student for immediate employment. This includes in-depth study of problems linked to the design of telecommunication networks (geographic, metropolitan, local areas), different transmission solutions, network architectures, protocols, and application fields. It will investigate standards and emerging protocols, analyzing achievable performance under changing design choices at each level of the protocol architecture. Much of the course is devoted to the TCP/IP architecture, from native protocols to the latest RFCs and their use in various network architectures.

To be able to make informed choices based on quality of service and traffic characteristics required by specific applications, and to use this knowledge for the development and implementation of efficient solutions in different application contexts. In general, to evaluate, analyze, and solve problems in new and emerging areas using modern technologies. This aims at short-term employment and provides a strong basis for graduated students.

To be able to understand the issues involved, apply acquired knowledge, propose solutions, and learn new planning methodologies, management, and monitoring of TLC networks. Specifically, students will deepen practical aspects by designing basic network components, configuring equipment and systems, monitoring elementary networks, designing and testing TLC services, and performing analysis, design, and management of systems for information treatment, transmission, and processing. Laboratory use of network simulators and communication devices, along with creating and testing simple communication systems, will develop cross-skills in ICT disciplines (electronics, computer science, signal theory, electromagnetic fields, antennas). Students will thus be able to use, develop, and manage disparate technologies and skills within broader contexts related to their field of study.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical, electrical, functional and procedural characteristics of some typical interfaces
Notes on X.25, ISDN and B-ISDN, Frame Relay and ATM
Standard Bluetooth: Bluetooth Low Energy, Beacon Bluetooth, Bluetooth 5.0

assessment_methods.method: Presentation and discussion of an optional project

assessment_rules: The learning assessment is through a verbal examination, optionally including the presentation and discussion of a project. The verbal examination is evaluated with a score out of thirty, with a minimum of eighteen points required for a positive evaluation. Students must demonstrate overall knowledge of topics, correct presentation, and use of proper technical terminology. For the maximum score, students must show a thorough understanding of topics and mastery of technical language. Praise is awarded for correct performance and particular brilliance.
